Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on PromptSmith's customer mix. We're interested in a focused "SDK retrofit" sprint to ensure Redwood's tracing / observability hooks and our LangChain / LlamaIndex shims work end-to-end for two of your reference apps.

Goals I want to align on before we lock the kickoff:
- Clear trace correlation between PromptSmith SDK calls and Redwood inference spans (request -> model token spans -> response)
- Out-of-the-box compatibility for LangChain v0.0x and LlamaIndex v1.x (we'll validate against your sample apps)
- Quickstart examples and a one-page integration guide for your engineers
- Automation tests in our sandbox for regressions on kernel and prompt changes

Attached is a short scope draft with proposed acceptance criteria and a proposed 2-week sprint timeline. Can you confirm: (1) which two customer apps you want prioritized, (2) a sample workload or prompt corpus we can run (if you prefer not to attach here, a secure upload link is fine), and (3) your availability for a 60-min kickoff week of June 7?

We can cover tracer span names and required attributes on the kickoff; tagging and PIIs will be handled per your security notes.

Thanks,

Thanks — quick technical plan and risks: 

Plan (high level):
- Instrumentation surface: provide a lightweight shim that exposes a single instrumentation entrypoint (redwood.trace.start_request) and an adapter for LangChain "LLM" classes and LlamaIndex connectors.
- Spans: request (high level) -> model.invocation (per token batch) -> cache/hit -> response assemble. Each model.invocation span should include model_name, quantization_profile, batch_size, token_count, and a timing_ms metric.
- Token timing: we should emit aggregated timing for token batches rather than per-token spans to keep trace volume reasonable; Oliver asked for token-level timing for hotspots — we'll provide both (aggregated by default, per-token optionally) and a toggle in the shim.
- Compatibility: implement adapters for LangChain agent and LlamaIndex Retriever APIs; where upstream APIs differ across versions, we'll include a small compatibility layer that detects version and adapts calls.

Risks/blockers:
- Customers running older LangChain agent patterns (pre-agent refactor) may require extra mapping work.
- Tokenization differences (model tokenizer vs app tokenizer) could skew timing — we'll add tokenizer checksum validation in tests.
- If PromptSmith needs per-token spans for every token in high-QPS traffic, sampling will be required to avoid telemetry cost blowup.

Estimate: 5 dev-days (shim + adapters) + 2 QA-days (sandbox tests & tokenizer validation) + 1 doc-day. If we need deep compatibility across three major LangChain versions, add ~3 dev-days.

Action items I will take before kickoff:
- Draft span naming and attribute checklist (will upload to the Google doc linked below)
- Prepare a minimal shim prototype for the kickoff demo (local run)

-Karthik
